title: Camera-trap detections of 15 mammal species at 210 Mojave Desert sites, California, 2016: nights with a detection out of nights surveyed
creator: Rich, Lindsey N.; Furnas, Brett J.; Newton, D. Scott; Brashares, Justin S.
citation: Rich, L. N., Furnas, B. J., Newton, D. S., & Brashares, J. S. (2019). Data from: Acoustic and camera surveys inform models of current and future vertebrate distributions in a changing desert ecosystem [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.2806394
abstract: Camera-trap survey of 15 mammal species at 210 sites in the Mojave Desert, California, March to July 2016 (Rich et al. 2019): the number of nights with a detection out of the nights surveyed per site and species, with seven site covariates.
samplingProtocol: Unbaited camera traps at 210 sites, one deployment per site (26-64 nights), March to July 2016; mammals identified to species from photographs; detections collapsed by the authors to nights with a detection per site and species.
surveyEvidenceNote: Every site has an explicit count for every deposited species and its nights surveyed (num.nights); which nights were surveyed is not deposited, so there is no occasion column (ruling #34).
closureNote: single season; one deployment per site, which the authors analysed as single-season multispecies occupancy
geographicCoverage: Mojave Desert, California, USA; no coordinates deposited

notShipped.Julian day squared: the square of Julian day (asserted), a model term

notes: Scientific names are the processor's, from the deposited common names (SpeciesCodes sheet). Julian day and background noise are site-level values as deposited (non-integer Julian days suggest a mean over visits). The other table from this deposit is rich_2019_mojave_birds_binom (acoustic).
